# Reception Perception: The Show — 2024-02-13

**Raw transcript:** `raw/ingested/reception-perception/2024-02-13-rp-chiefs-take-down-49ers-for-super-bowl-lviii.md` (immutable — do not edit)

## Summary

With co-host **James Koh** (not tracked). A Super Bowl LVIII recap (Chiefs 25,
49ers 22, OT) plus an early offseason-outlook segment for both rosters. Last
episode of the 2023 season — the show is taking a week off before pivoting
fully to free agency and the 2024 draft class.

**Game recap.** Pushes back on "Shanahan abandoned the run" criticism of
[[Christian McCaffrey]]'s second-half usage as results-driven hindsight —
McCaffrey still touched the ball 30 times, and Kansas City's blitz-heavy plan
(via a Steven Ruiz/LeJarius Sneed postgame exchange) was designed to make
Brock Purdy throw. Frames [[Deebo Samuel]]'s quiet game (11 targets, 3
catches, 33 yards) as the Chiefs defense executing a specific, deliberate
plan — pressing him at the line to take away the zone/YAC role that's his
real strength while live with Brandon Aiyuk beating them on a couple of
in-breakers instead — a fresh, game-level confirmation of Harmon's own
long-standing man-vs-zone read on Samuel. [[Brock Purdy]] gets a
continuation of Harmon's "good, not elite" grade: no "wow" throws, overstated
accuracy reputation, and an explicit comp to the Jared Goff/Kirk Cousins
archetype — a player whose physical tools are what they are, whose growth
has to come from pre/post-snap processing catching up with experience, the
same trajectory Harmon credits [[Patrick Mahomes]] with already having
completed. [[Patrick Mahomes]] gets Harmon's most unqualified praise yet —
399 total yards against a defense-first opponent with no healthy outside
receivers, framed as the best quarterback in football because he rarely
misdiagnoses coverage before the snap, escapes pressure at an elite rate, and
has no real holes to nitpick. [[Travis Kelce]] gets credit for effectively
carrying the KC passing game alone in the second half/OT (1 target for 1 yard
in the first half, 8-for-92 the rest of the way). [[Isiah Pacheco]]'s box
score (18-59, 3.3 YPC) is read as evidence of how inconsistent Kansas City's
run-blocking was all year, not as a talent read on the back himself.

**Offseason outlook.** For Kansas City: the receiver room (McCole Hardman,
Marquez Valdes-Scantling, Justin Watson, [[Skyy Moore]]) needs a clean-slate
rebuild around a true X — Harmon wants a man-coverage-beating, contested-catch
receiver, explicitly not another "zone-beating" name like [[Marquise Brown]]
(nicknamed "Hollywood"), and names [[Brian Thomas Jr.]] as a draft-class fit
for the vertical-X role. [[Rashee Rice]] is flagged as "a fascinating player
to discuss and debate" this offseason — Harmon points to his own (separate,
non-podcast) YouTube mailbag for a fuller rookie-year comp to
[[Amon-Ra St. Brown]]. Also floats [[Brandon Aiyuk]] as a name he'd inquire
about in a hypothetical trade (while doubting he's realistically available)
and flags Aiyuk as "woefully underpaid" on his fifth-year option. For San
Francisco: reads 2023 as a nearly-everything-broke-right season the roster
likely can't repeat, and calls out a coming, unavoidable roster crunch — not
all three of [[George Kittle]], [[Brandon Aiyuk]] and [[Deebo Samuel]] survive
to 2025 given the cap picture, with Aiyuk's underpaid fifth-year option and
[[Christian McCaffrey]] entering the run-back age range flagged as the two
sharpest near-term risk points.
